definition: to increase suddenly and by a large amount
exampleIELTS: Online sales surged from 12% in 2010 to 38% in 2020, overtaking in-store purchases.

definition: to fall or drop straight down at high speed
exampleIELTS: Coal consumption plummeted from 60 million tonnes to barely 15 million over the period shown.

definition: to rise quickly to a high level
exampleIELTS: The number of international tourists soared, reaching a peak of 2.1 million in 2018.

definition: to stop rising or falling and remain at a steady level
exampleIELTS: After a sharp rise in the first decade, female participation plateaued at around 65%.

definition: to change frequently in size, amount, or quality
exampleIELTS: Unemployment fluctuated between 4% and 7% throughout the period, with no clear upward or downward trend.

definition: to become steady and stop changing
exampleIELTS: Carbon emissions stabilised at approximately 30 megatonnes from 2015 onwards.

definition: to reach the highest level before falling
exampleIELTS: Energy consumption peaked at 850 terawatt-hours in 2008 before declining steadily thereafter.

definition: a small, temporary fall in a level or amount
exampleIELTS: Despite a brief dip in 2015, overall production rose throughout the period.

definition: to rise gradually over time
exampleIELTS: Tuition fees climbed steadily from £3,000 in 2005 to over £9,000 by 2020.

definition: to gradually become smaller or weaker
exampleIELTS: Newspaper readership dwindled over the two decades, falling from 75% to under 30%.

definition: to a large extent or degree
exampleIELTS: The proportion of households owning a smartphone rose substantially, from 23% to 91% over the period.

definition: by a very small amount
exampleIELTS: Public transport usage rose only marginally, by about two percentage points across the decade.

definition: as judged in comparison with something else
exampleIELTS: Spending on healthcare was comparatively high, almost double that of any other category.

definition: in a way that corresponds in size or amount to something else
exampleIELTS: Although Japan's population is smaller, it consumed proportionally more energy per capita than India.

definition: by a sudden and very large amount
exampleIELTS: Renewable energy use increased dramatically, more than tripling between 2000 and 2020.

definition: at a regular and constant rate
exampleIELTS: Car ownership rose steadily across the period, gaining around two percentage points each year.

definition: suddenly and unexpectedly
exampleIELTS: The downward trend ended abruptly in 2018, when figures recovered to pre-recession levels.

definition: the lowest point in a fluctuating series of values
exampleIELTS: Sales reached a trough of just 4,000 units in 2012 before recovering throughout the rest of the decade.

definition: a part or share of a whole
exampleIELTS: A growing proportion of commuters chose cycling over driving during the period shown.

definition: a noticeable difference between two things that should match
exampleIELTS: There is a marked discrepancy between male and female enrolment in engineering, with men outnumbering women three to one.

definition: the overall pattern or path of change over time
exampleIELTS: The two countries followed a similar trajectory, with both seeing rapid urban growth after 2005.

definition: of considerable importance, size, or worth
exampleIELTS: The chart shows a substantial increase in renewable energy use between 2010 and 2020.

definition: so small or unimportant that it can be ignored
exampleIELTS: The change in coal use was negligible, varying by less than one percent across the entire period.

definition: easy to see or recognise
exampleIELTS: There was a noticeable shift towards online shopping, particularly among younger consumers.

definition: following one after another in unbroken sequence
exampleIELTS: Emissions fell for three consecutive years before rising again in the final period.

definition: to publicly recommend or support a particular policy or idea
exampleIELTS: While many advocate stricter regulation of social media, others argue that this would infringe on freedom of expression.

definition: to assert something firmly as a position in argument
exampleIELTS: Critics contend that increased automation will displace millions of low-skilled workers within a generation.

definition: to regard something as caused by a particular factor
exampleIELTS: The decline in obesity rates can largely be attributed to public health campaigns and stricter food labelling.

definition: to make a problem or bad situation worse
exampleIELTS: Banning private vehicles in city centres may exacerbate inequality, as poorer residents often live further from public transport.

definition: to make something bad less severe or harmful
exampleIELTS: Investment in renewable energy is essential if we are to mitigate the worst effects of climate change.

definition: to make a problem or suffering less intense
exampleIELTS: Conditional cash transfers have helped alleviate extreme poverty in several Latin American countries.

definition: to encourage the development of something
exampleIELTS: Schools should foster critical thinking from an early age rather than rewarding mere memorisation.

definition: to gradually weaken something, especially authority or confidence
exampleIELTS: Excessive screen time risks undermining children's ability to concentrate on extended tasks.

definition: to make something, especially a problem or belief, continue indefinitely
exampleIELTS: Stereotypes in advertising can perpetuate harmful gender norms in the workplace.

definition: to delay or make difficult the progress of something
exampleIELTS: Excessive bureaucracy continues to hinder the adoption of telemedicine in rural communities.

definition: to show or prove to be right or reasonable
exampleIELTS: Proponents argue that the financial cost of space exploration is justified by the technological spin-offs it produces.

definition: to reject something as unimportant or invalid
exampleIELTS: It would be a mistake to dismiss the concerns of parents regarding online safety simply as moral panic.

definition: to prove that a statement or theory is wrong
exampleIELTS: Recent longitudinal studies have refuted the claim that streaming services reduce attention span in adolescents.

definition: to treat something as more important than other matters
exampleIELTS: Governments should prioritise long-term environmental protection over short-term economic gains.

definition: the position or attitude one publicly takes on a matter
exampleIELTS: The author adopts a critical stance towards the privatisation of higher education.

definition: general agreement among a group
exampleIELTS: There is a clear scientific consensus that human activity is the dominant cause of recent global warming.

definition: the underlying reason or logic for a decision or belief
exampleIELTS: The rationale for taxing sugary drinks is straightforward: to discourage consumption of products linked to obesity.

definition: strongly persuasive; difficult to argue against
exampleIELTS: There is a compelling argument that universal basic income would simplify welfare and reduce administrative costs.

definition: harmful or causing damage
exampleIELTS: Excessive use of antibiotics has proven detrimental to long-term gut health in young children.

definition: certain to happen; unavoidable
exampleIELTS: Some degree of automation in the manufacturing sector now appears inevitable.

definition: more important than anything else
exampleIELTS: When designing public spaces, accessibility for people with disabilities should be paramount.

definition: having the opposite effect to the one intended
exampleIELTS: Excessively strict drug laws can be counterproductive, pushing users away from treatment programmes.

definition: possible future effects or consequences of an action
exampleIELTS: The widespread adoption of remote work has profound implications for urban housing markets.

definition: a balance between two desirable but incompatible features
exampleIELTS: There is a clear trade-off between economic growth and environmental protection in many emerging economies.

definition: to support or form the basis of an argument or system
exampleIELTS: Trust between citizens and institutions underpins every well-functioning democracy.

definition: used to add a further point that strengthens what was just said
exampleIELTS: Public transport is more efficient than private cars; furthermore, it produces significantly less pollution per passenger.

definition: used to add information that strengthens or extends the previous point
exampleIELTS: Working from home reduces commuting time; moreover, it allows employees greater control over their schedule.

definition: used to compare two things and emphasise their difference
exampleIELTS: France relies heavily on nuclear power, whereas Germany, by contrast, has invested predominantly in renewables.

definition: used to introduce a contrasting view or aspect
exampleIELTS: Online learning offers flexibility; on the other hand, it can leave less motivated students isolated.

definition: introducing a statement that reverses the one just made
exampleIELTS: Higher taxes on tobacco reduce consumption; conversely, lowering them has historically led to a rise in smoking rates.

definition: in spite of what has just been said
exampleIELTS: The proposal has clear flaws; nonetheless, it represents a step in the right direction.

definition: as a logical or direct result of something
exampleIELTS: Many young adults postpone home ownership; consequently, the average age of first-time buyers has risen sharply.

definition: in a way that is suitable to the circumstances; therefore
exampleIELTS: Demand for plant-based products has grown rapidly, and supermarkets have adjusted their offerings accordingly.

definition: because of; due to
exampleIELTS: Owing to falling birth rates, several European countries are now relying heavily on immigration to maintain their workforce.

definition: taking into account; given that
exampleIELTS: In light of recent scientific findings, several governments have updated their dietary guidelines.

definition: used to introduce a specific example
exampleIELTS: Many countries have moved towards cashless economies; Sweden, for instance, expects to eliminate physical currency by 2030.

definition: used to introduce an example that clarifies the previous point
exampleIELTS: Renewable energy is now cost-competitive. To illustrate, the price of solar power has fallen by almost 90% in a decade.

definition: an especially clear example that proves the point being made
exampleIELTS: Some cities have transformed their air quality through bold policy. London's ultra-low emission zone is a case in point.
collocations: is a clear case in point

definition: used to acknowledge something that weakens your point, before answering it
exampleIELTS: Admittedly, electric vehicles still have a sizeable carbon footprint at production; however, their lifecycle emissions remain far lower than those of petrol cars.

definition: used to acknowledge a point before pushing back on it
exampleIELTS: Granted, social media can spread misinformation; even so, it remains a crucial tool for civic engagement.

definition: considering all the arguments together; overall
exampleIELTS: On balance, the benefits of compulsory voting outweigh the practical drawbacks for most established democracies.
collocations: on balance, it is fair to say

definition: used to express a strong but not certain opinion
exampleIELTS: Climate change is arguably the most pressing collective challenge of the twenty-first century.

definition: as appears to be the case, though perhaps not really so
exampleIELTS: The policy is ostensibly designed to protect consumers, although critics suggest its primary aim is political.

definition: in spite of; without being prevented by
exampleIELTS: Notwithstanding recent improvements, the gender pay gap remains a stubborn feature of most labour markets.

definition: although; even though (used to introduce a qualifying clause)
exampleIELTS: Living standards continued to improve, albeit at a slower pace than in previous decades.

definition: mostly; largely true but with some qualification
exampleIELTS: To a large extent, individual habits are shaped by the environment in which a person grows up.

definition: considering everything; in general
exampleIELTS: On the whole, students who learn a second language before adolescence achieve a more native-like accent.

definition: concerning; in relation to a particular topic
exampleIELTS: With regard to childhood obesity, school nutrition policies have proved more effective than public awareness campaigns.

definition: used to summarise the central point of an argument
exampleIELTS: In essence, the debate is not about whether technology should be regulated, but about how.

definition: used to introduce a brief summary at the end of an argument
exampleIELTS: To sum up, while urbanisation has clear economic benefits, it places considerable strain on housing and infrastructure.

definition: to be or form the parts that together make up something
exampleIELTS: Women constitute almost 60% of higher education graduates in most OECD countries.

definition: to consist of; to be made up of
exampleIELTS: The committee comprises representatives from all twelve member states.

definition: to include a wide range of related things
exampleIELTS: Sustainable development encompasses environmental, economic and social dimensions, all of which must be balanced.

definition: to emphasise the importance of something
exampleIELTS: The recent pandemic has underscored the need for resilient public health systems.

definition: to produce a result, profit, or finding
exampleIELTS: Investment in early childhood education yields long-term returns far exceeding its initial cost.

definition: to strengthen or further support an idea, system or feeling
exampleIELTS: Repeated exposure to advertising reinforces consumer brand loyalty.

definition: to confirm or support a finding with additional evidence
exampleIELTS: Three independent studies have corroborated the link between air pollution and reduced cognitive function.

definition: to add something to enhance or complete it
exampleIELTS: Many universities now supplement traditional lectures with interactive online modules.

definition: to become apparent or come into existence
exampleIELTS: A consensus has begun to emerge among economists regarding the long-term impact of automation on wages.

definition: to develop gradually, especially in response to changing conditions
exampleIELTS: The role of universities has evolved considerably since the rise of online learning platforms.

definition: to change something completely and fundamentally
exampleIELTS: Mobile banking has revolutionised access to financial services in much of sub-Saharan Africa.

definition: to accept the truth or existence of something
exampleIELTS: Even critics acknowledge that public transport investment has reduced inner-city congestion.

definition: a situation or fact that is observed to exist, especially one whose cause is being studied
exampleIELTS: The phenomenon of language attrition is increasingly common among second-generation immigrants.

definition: a typical pattern or model that defines how something is understood
exampleIELTS: The shift from ownership to access is a paradigm shift that has reshaped industries from music to transport.

definition: a distinctive feature or characteristic of something
exampleIELTS: Transparency and accountability are the hallmarks of a healthy democracy.

definition: an event or person that causes a significant change
exampleIELTS: The financial crisis acted as a catalyst for reforms in banking regulation worldwide.

definition: the most essential part of something
exampleIELTS: Free and impartial journalism remains a cornerstone of any functioning democracy.

definition: a hidden or unsuspected difficulty
exampleIELTS: One pitfall of self-reported survey data is that respondents tend to overestimate socially desirable behaviours.

definition: spreading widely throughout an area or group
exampleIELTS: Misinformation has become pervasive on social media, posing a serious challenge to public discourse.

definition: existing as a permanent and essential characteristic
exampleIELTS: There is an inherent tension between economic growth and environmental sustainability.

definition: very great or intense; far-reaching
exampleIELTS: The internet has had a profound impact on how young people form social relationships.

definition: clear and concrete enough to be measured or seen
exampleIELTS: Investment in cycling infrastructure has produced tangible benefits in air quality and public health.

definition: marked by subtle distinctions and shades of meaning
exampleIELTS: A more nuanced view of immigration recognises both its economic contributions and the pressures it places on services.

definition: most noticeable or important
exampleIELTS: The most salient feature of the chart is the dramatic decline in newspaper readership after 2010.

definition: never done or known before
exampleIELTS: Remote work was adopted at an unprecedented scale during the pandemic, permanently reshaping office norms.
